SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fiberglass Structural Repair

 Fiberglass Repair 

 Safety Precautions 

 WARNING: ALWAYS WORK IN A WELL-VENTILATED AREA IN ORDER TO AVOID POSSIBLE TOXIC 
FUMES THAT MAY RESULT FROM USING RESIN MIXTURES. EXERCISE CARE SO AS NOT TO 
GET ANY RESIN ON CLOTHING. 

 CAUTION: Remove any resin from hands as soon as possible and particularly before 
the mixture starts to gel. 

Always use rubber gloves or the special hand cream supplied with epoxy 
resin repair kits. Any resin that adheres to the hands may be removed with 
lacquer thinner followed by a thorough washing with soap and water.

Use a respirator when grinding the surface and use a vacuum attachment 
when operating a belt sander.

Keep all materials, utensils and the work area clean and dry as resin 
repairs involve chemical reactions. Any dirt, foreign material or moisture may 
upset the chemical reaction and result in an unsatisfactory repair.

 Repair Procedure 

Grind or sand away all loose or broken material at the damaged area. 
Scuff sand the surface approximately 25mm (1 inch) around the area to provide 
a good bonding surface. Make sure the surface to be repaired is clean, dry, 
oil and paint free.

For cracks, form a shallow V-shape along the crack with a file or 
grinder. Fill the area with a good quality body repair compound. Follow the 
manufacturer's directions with regard to mixing procedures. Allow the compound 
to harden and then sand smooth. If the surface is not level or smooth, use an 
additional filling and sand to a final smooth finish.

For larger broken areas use fiberglass cloth (five layers) impregnated 
with the resin, to cover the area. Overlap the damaged portion by 25-50mm (1-2 
inches). When the material has hardened, file or grind and sand smooth. If low 
spots exist, fill them with resin mixture to which short fibers cut from the 
fiberglass cloth have been added. Add enough of the cloth to form a putty-like 
resin mixture.

 Painting 

After the desired repaired surface has been obtained, prime and paint 
the surface in the normal manner.

 Repairs From Backside (Procedure A) 

Components with large cracked or broken areas must be repaired from the 
backside first. Perform backside repairs following fiberglass repair procedure 
in this section.

When backside repair is completed, repeat operation on front side of 
component.

 Backside Not Accessible 

Should vehicle component requiring backside repair not permit access to 
backside, it must be removed from vehicle to perform repair. Use extreme 
caution when repairing components while off the vehicle to ensure proper 
alignment when reinstalling repaired component on the vehicle.

Follow all procedures previously outlined in this section.

 Cosmetic Repair (Procedure B) 

Minor damage (damage which does not affect the structural integrity of 
the component) is considered a cosmetic repair and is performed on the 
exterior of the component only. Perform these repairs using the following 
procedure.

Grind or sand away all loose or broken material at the damaged area.

Remove all paint approximately 50mm (2 inches) around the area to 
provide a good bonding surface. Make sure the surface to be repaired is clean, 
dry and oil free.

Form a shallow V-shape along cracks with a file or grinder.

Fill the area with a good quality epoxy based body repair compound. 
Follow the manufacturer's guidelines for proper mixing procedures.

Allow the compound to harden and sand to the proper contour. Use 
additional compound if the surface is not smooth, level and to contour.

Prime and top coat following paint manufacturers label instructions.

 Laminate Separation (Procedure C) 

Occasionally fiberglass components may experience laminate separation 
damage. This condition can be repaired following the cosmetic repair 
procedures previously outlined providing the extent of laminate separation is 
not too severe. If the laminate separation condition is extensive it may be 
more practical to replace the component.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Paint Damage from Airborne Materials

The following information gives detailed descriptions of paint damage 
caused by chemical or organic materials. If service is required, identify the 
source of the damage and follow the recommended service procedure.

 Chemical 

The effects of chemical airborne materials can be seen as:

Dark blotches in the paint where the pigment in the paint surface has 
been attacked.

Irregular spots that are cracked or etched around the edges and dull in 
the centers.

Small orange colored spots caused by iron particles may appear on the 
paint surface.

Generally, materials that attack a paint film are either acidic or 
alkaline in nature.

Sulfuric and nitric acids, in general, cause extreme damage to 
automotive paint finishes. Even very small concentrations of the same 
materials can cause chemical spotting damage. Due to evaporation and 
condensation, these acids can create severe etching "spots" that may 
eventually crack or lift the paint film after some time in service.

Although some automotive finishes are more resistant than others, none 
are completely immune to these chemicals. The most resistant paints used today 
are the urethanes because their resin system is least likely to react with 
chemicals. Air-dry coatings are more susceptible to attack only when they are 
fresh. The longer the paint dries the more resistant it becomes.

Metallic colors are more intolerant to chemicals because aluminum flake 
is fairly reactive with either an acid or alkali.

The following pH chart shows the relationship between acidic and 
alkaline chemicals and their corresponding pH values. This chart is provided 
for informational reference only.

 ACIDS/ALKALIES AND pH CHART

pH Scale Value

Examples

2.0 — Very Strong Acids

Hydrochloric, Nitric Sulfuric, Phosphoric, Hydrofluoric and Some Wire
Wheel Cleaners

3.0 — Strong Acids

Citric, Chromic, Sulfonic, and Human Gastric Juices

4.0 — Acidic

Oxalic, Gluconic, Tartaric Fallout Remover

5.0 — Slightly Acidic

Lactic, Uric, Acid Rain

6.0 — Very Slightly Acidic

Carbonic

7.0 — Neutral

Blood, Most Body Fluids, 

 Distilled Water

8.0 — Very Slightly Alkaline

Urine, Wash Concentrate

9.0 — Slightly Alkaline

Baking Soda

10.0 — Alkaline

Soda Ash, Carb-Kleen

11.0 — Strong Alkaline

Lye, Potash, Tire Cleaner

 Organic 

Organic damage is generally easier to identify. Organic damage is 
mostly due to tree sap, bird and insect droppings, dead insects and pollen. 
Tree sap is easily identified by clear raised drops that may be hard or 
sticky. Bee or bug dropping spots may appear brownish or yellow in color, 
about 3-6mm (1/8 to 1/4 inch) in diameter. Dead and decomposing insect bodies 
are readily visible to the eye. Pollen deposits are small yellow clusters. 
Each of these items is potentially damage to any currently available paint 
system. Other noticeable traits of organic damage are spots that are raised 
(swelling), micro-crazing (cracked) and pitting due to pollen eating into the 
paint film. The active ingredients in most organic contaminants are tannic and 
formic acids. These acids are found in berries and bodily fluids of insects 
and birds.

Investigations completed at dealerships show that the bright lot lights 
tend to attract insects. The use of "soft lights" for display and storage lot 
illumination will help reduce damage resulting from decomposing bugs and 
droppings by decreasing the number of bugs attracted to these lights. Organic 
damage is accelerated by heat. During very hot weather conditions, it is 
important to wash vehicles more often.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Chemical or Organic Damage Repair

Iron dust particles may imbed themselves into the paint film. On some 
light colored vehicles after some weathering, tiny dots of rust start to 
appear. They feel rough to the touch and are difficult to remove. The best way 
to remove these particles is by treating the finish with a 
multi-acid-detergent-water wash. Use the following procedure to perform this 
service repair.

 NOTE: Acid washes are also prepackaged in various strengths under various 
brand names.

 CAUTION: Do not use oxalic acid washes. This material will damage paint and trim 
if used incorrectly. Use only multi-acid washes such as Finish Kare for 
removal of iron particles. Follow manufacturers mixing instructions. 

Wash and degrease the vehicle first, using Ford Multi-Purpose Cleaner 
Concentrate B8A-19523-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P4-A, 
and a suitable wax and grease remover. If this does not remove all of the iron 
particles, proceed with the acid wash.

Apply this solution liberally to all affected surfaces of the vehicle 
with a large sponge. Keep the surface wet until the technician can no longer 
feel any surface roughness with bare or gloved fingertips. If this is not done 
thoroughly, staining may redevelop if iron particles are left behind.

 CAUTION: Failure to thoroughly rinse this surface could result in corrosion of 
anodized aluminum or stainless steel parts with prolonged contact. 

Rinse the area with clean water.

If the iron particles are not totally removed after two washings, use 
one or both of the procedures listed for minor chemical contamination.

The use of polishing (with wax), sanding with microfine sandpaper (1500 
grit or greater) or buffing with very light compound should only be done as a 
last resort.

 Wet Sanding — After Acid Wash 

Clean the exterior surface of the vehicle with Ford Multi-Purpose 
Cleaner Concentrate B8A-19523-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M14P4-A to remove all contamination.

Apply 1500 grit sandpaper to a rubber padded sanding block to sand the 
paint surface.

Use a squirt bottle filled with water to lubricate the 1500 grit 
sandpaper as you begin to sand only the damaged areas. Water is an abrasive as 
well as a lubricant in this step.

If the damage has gone deeply into the paint film and it will not 
polish or sand out, then refinishing is required.

 Paint Reconditioning 

Acrylic urethane enamel base/clear paint systems should be painted by 
using the following procedure.

Prepare the area as follows:

Neutralize the affected areas with baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) and 
water.

Rinse the surface off with plain water.

Wash the panel with a mild soapy detergent.

Dry the panel completely.

If the damage is through the top coat finish and into the primers, the 
panel must be sanded down to bare metal or plastic and then refinished.

Apply a self-etching primer for metal surfaces only .

A flex additive may be necessary when working with flexible plastics. 
Then proceed as follows:

Apply a two component urethane primer surfacer. Let dry per instructions.

Sand the surface with 400 grit sandpaper to get proper finish.

Finish sanding with 600 grit sandpaper.

Solvent wash the panel with wax and grease remover. Tack wipe it.

The use of acrylic urethane enamel is highly recommended for this type 
of repair.

Apply base coat or top coat material per applicable paint system.

Apply clear acrylic urethane if you are using a base/clear paint system.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Floorpan Plugs and Grommets

Many plugs and grommets are used in the floorpan and dash panel. The 
floorpan plugs seal the various access holes. If any plugs are missing or 
improperly installed, a dust or water leak may result. This also applies to 
the grommets used on the dash panel. When dust or water leaks are evident, 
these plugs and grommets should be checked for proper installation.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Drain Holes

 NOTE: Check the drain holes regularly. Clean dirt and foreign material from 
the drain holes with a punch or screwdriver.

Drain holes are located on the underside of each door along the weld 
line of the inner and outer panels. If these holes become clogged with mud or 
road tars, water will collect inside the panels and rust the sheet metal from 
the inside. A sound of sloshing water in a door is an indication of this 
condition.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Rattle Elimination

Foreign objects such as nuts, bolts or small pieces of body deadener in 
the door wells, pillars and quarter panels, are often the source of rattles. 
Door wells can be checked by carefully striking the underside of the door with 
a rubber mallet.

All bolts and screws should be inspected periodically. In the event 
that tightening the bolts and screws, located on such assemblies as the doors, 
hood, and luggage compartment deck lid, does not eliminate the rattles, the 
trouble is probably caused by misalignment. If this is the case, Refer to Section 01-02 
and Section 01-03 .

Rattles and squeaks are sometimes caused by weatherstripping and 
anti-squeak material that has slipped out of position. Apply additional cement 
or other adhesive.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Trim

Periodic cleaning will preserve the beauty and life of bright metals. 
Wash with clear water, or if the parts are very dirty, use Multi-Purpose 
Cleaner Concentrate B8A-19523-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M14P4-A. Using a clean, soft cloth or a sponge and water, rinse and wipe 
the parts dry. Custom Bright Metal Cleaner 8A-19522-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESR-M5B194-B, may be used sparingly to remove salt, road 
chemicals and corrosion deposits from chrome-plated parts. Do not scour 
aluminum or chrome finished parts with steel wool or polish them with products 
containing abrasives. Custom Silicone Gloss Polish B7AZ-19530-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M11B26-A will provide excellent protection for 
all bright metal parts.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Body Maintenance 

Regular body maintenance preserves the vehicle's appearance during the 
life of the vehicle. The following steps are suggested as a guide for regular 
body maintenance:

Vacuum interior thoroughly and wash the vehicle. 

Check all openings for water leaks and seal where necessary. 

Cement all usable, loose weatherstrips, using Weatherstrip Adhesive 
E8AZ-19552-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G14-A.

Replace all door and luggage compartment deck lid weatherstrips which 
are damaged or worn.

Apply Silicone Lubricant C0AZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M13P4-A, to the weatherstripping.

Replace all cracked, fogged, or chipped glass. 

Align hood, doors and deck lid if necessary. 

Inspect windshield wiper blades and replace if necessary. 

Tighten the scuff plate and garnish moulding screws. Refer to Section 01-05A or Section 01-05B .

Clean seats, door trim panels and headlining. 

Apply touch-up paint to chipped or scratched areas. 

Drain holes should be cleared periodically.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Underbody Heat Deflectors 

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle and secure with Rotunda Car/Truck Stands 077-00018 or 
equivalent. 

Remove all components necessary to gain access to heat deflectors. 

Using a correct size drill bit, drill out the heat deflector rivets. 

Remove the heat deflectors. 

 Installation 

Align the heat deflector rivet holes with their corresponding holes. 

Install rivets using Rotunda Blind Fastener Installation Tool 107-R0600 
or equivalent. Make sure floor holes are properly sealed after rivets are 
installed. 

Install components that were removed to access heat deflectors. 

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Underbody

Clean the underbody and, if necessary, remove undercoating in all 
suspect areas of the underbody. Inspect for visible damage. Inspect underbody 
for any loose fasteners and excessive gaps which may contribute to air, dust 
or water leaks. Repair loose fasteners and/or seal gaps with appropriate 
sealers. Refer to Section 01-00 . In the case of a collision-damaged vehicle, the vehicle underbody 
should also be inspected for secondary damage due to collision energy 
management engineering.

================================================================================
PAGE 3445
================================================================================
1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-01: Underbody

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Body Misalignment Check

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to correct any serious misalignment with one jacking 
operation. This is particularly true if other sections of the body also 
require aligning. Align each section proportionately until the proper 
dimensions are obtained. 

To align or square up a body, take two opposite diagonal measurements 
between pillars. Use a measuring tram for these measurements. Take the 
measurements between reference points such as crease lines or weld joints 
which are diagonally opposite each other on the two pillars being measured. 
Since all measurements should be made from the bare metal, remove all interior 
trim from the checking points. 

In some cases, it is difficult to obtain proper body alignment when 
repairing a body that is damaged on both sides. In these cases, horizontal and 
vertical measurements can be taken from a body of the same body style. Once 
these basic dimensions are taken and established on the damaged body, 
alignment can be made by diagonal measurements taken from points on the two 
pillars. 

Door openings are checked in the same manner as the body. Horizontal, 
vertical, and diagonal checking points are established on all four sides of 
the door opening that is being measured.

ADJUSTMENTS

Straightening Operations

Misalignment can be corrected by straightening the out-of-line parts or 
by replacing the crossmembers, braces, or brackets if they are badly damaged.

Straightening should be attempted on frames that fail to meet 
specification of the diagonal checking method or where damage is visually 
apparent.

 CAUTION: If heat is needed to straighten a frame member, keep the temperature 
below 649°C (1200°F) (a dull red glow). 
Excessive heat may weaken the metal and cause permanent damage. 

However, to prevent internal stresses in the metal, straightening 
should be limited to parts which are not severely bent.

================================================================================
PAGE 3448
================================================================================
1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-01: Underbody

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment, Unitized Body, Aerostar

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to correct any serious misalignment with one jacking 
operation. This is particularly true if other sections of the body also 
require aligning. Align each section proportionately until the proper 
dimensions are obtained. 

To align or square-up a body, take two opposite diagonal measurements 
between pillars. Use a measuring tram for these measurements. Take the 
measurements between reference points such as crease lines or weld joints 
which are diagonally opposite each other on the two pillars being measured. 
Since all measurements should be made from the bare metal, remove all interior 
trim from the checking points.

In some cases, it is difficult to obtain proper body alignment when 
repairing a body that is damaged on both sides. In these cases, horizontal and 
vertical measurements can be taken from a body of the same body style. Once 
these basic dimensions are taken and established on the damaged body, 
alignment can be made by diagonal measurements taken from points on two pillars.

Door openings are checked in the same manner as the body. Horizontal, 
vertical, and diagonal checking points are established on all four sides of 
the door opening that is being measured.

Section 01-01: Underbody

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Welding

 CAUTION: Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301) (14301) before using any 
electrical welding equipment. 

Perform all welding using Rotunda MIG Wire Feed Welder 106-0053 or 
equivalent, and welding wire meeting AWS-E-70S specification.

Because more extensive panel deformation results from oxyacetylene 
welding than from MIG welding or spot welding, perform sectional welding using 
MIG welding or spot welding equipment only.

Perform spot welding operations in locations that are inaccessible with 
spot welding tongs using the plug weld method. Drill or punch 8mm (5/16-inch) 
holes in one side of the flange and weld.

Varying factors determine plate thickness, panel design, 
cross-sectionals and sizes, joining method, welding method, and welding 
locations during manufacturing. To apply the most suitable repair method, it 
is most important to completely understand the body design, concept, and 
construction.

It is essential that repair welds, particularly on load-bearing parts 
or parts contributing to the strength of the assembly, are equivalent to the 
originals in size, type, and strength.

 Low-Alloy Steel Components 

 NOTE: When cutting salvage or repairable components, use a grinding disc, air 
chisel, or metal cutting saw.

 NOTE: All welding should be done with a Rotunda MIG Wire Feed Welder 
106-00053 or equivalent with welding wire meeting AWS-E-70S specification.

 CAUTION: Disconnect the battery ground cable before using any electric welding 
equipment. 

Because of associated high heat buildup, do not use oxyacetylene when 
welding high-tensile or high-strength, low-alloy steel components. Use spot or 
MIG. During MIG welding, use a temperature-indicating crayon to ensure that 
the temperature does not exceed 750°C (1400°
F).

Replace spot-welded components by spot welding where possible. If spot 
welding equipment is not available, or if the location is not accessible, plug 
weld the panels.

Use MIG welding rather than conventional arc welding when welding 
high-strength, high-tensile, or conventional mild steel. Use .024 or .030 
diameter wire and conform to Classification AWS, E70S. MIG welding is also 
known as GMAW (Gas Metal Arc Welding).

DESCRIPTION

Hood Components

The hood (16612) is a front-opening type secured by a standard 
double-release hood latch (16700). The hood latch control handle and cable is 
located below and to the right of the steering column.

The hood pivots on two hood hinges (16796) and is held open by a hood 
support rod (16826). 

The hood can be aligned fore and aft and side to side by loosening the 
hinge bolts.

The hood insulator (16738) is attached with pushpins.

The radiator grille on Ranger is attached to the radiator grille 
opening panel (8190).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hood Latch, Aerostar 

 Removal 

Mark location of bracket for installation. 

Remove two hood latch attaching screws. 

Disconnect cable from latch, routing cable and fitting through return 
spring. 

Remove hood latch (16700). 

 Installation 

Maneuver hood release cable terminal through curled return spring on 
back side of hood latch.

Locate square cable bushing tab in hood latch housing keyhole slot and 
fasten screw snug, but do not overtighten 1.8-2.6 Nm (16-23 
lb-in).

Adjust the hood latch for positive engagement with the hood latch 
striker (16K689). Also, make sure that secondary hook engages hood latch 
striker smoothly. Tighten the latch attaching screws to 10-14 Nm
 (7-10 lb-ft). 

 NOTE: Make sure lubricant has effectively worked into the pivot points and 
bearing surfaces.

Lubricate the latch handle pivot, catch pawls and spring with 
Multi-Purpose Grease spray D7AZ-19584-AA, or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M1C106-B. Recheck the functional operation of the hood latch 
and safety latch by opening and closing the hood (16612) several times to make 
sure latch function is correct.

ADJUSTMENTS

Hood Alignment 

The hood (16612) can be adjusted fore and aft and side to side by 
loosening the hood-to-hinge attaching bolts and repositioning the hood. To 
raise or lower the hood, loosen the hinge hood-to-body attaching bolts and 
turn bumpers clockwise to lower or counterclockwise to raise.

ADJUSTMENTS

Hood Bumpers

Hood bumpers (16758) located on the top RH and top LH surfaces of the 
radiator support (16138) can be adjusted up and down to provide a flush 
surface alignment of the hood (16612) with the front fenders (16005).

1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-02: Body Panels, Front End

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Hood Latch

 NOTE: Before adjusting the hood latch (16700), make certain that the hood 
(16612) is properly aligned. The hood latch can be moved from side to side, up 
and down and laterally to obtain a snug fit. 

Loosen the hood latch attaching screws just enough to move the hood 
latch. 

Move the hood latch until it is aligned with the hood latch striker 
(16K689). Then, tighten the hood latch attaching screws. Check hood-to-fender 
fit.

Check the hood latch to make sure it makes full engagement with the 
hood latch striker. If the hood latch does not make full engagement with the 
hood latch striker, loosen the hood latch attaching screws and reposition the 
hood latch to obtain full engagement. Then, tighten the attaching screws. 

 NOTE: Make sure lubricant has effectively worked into the pivot points and 
bearing surfaces.

Lubricate the latch handle pivot, catch pawls and spring with 
Multi-Purpose Grease spray D7AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M1C106-B. Recheck the functional operation of the hood latch 
mechanism and safety latch by operating and closing the hood several times to 
make sure function is correct.

Section 01-03: Doors and Liftgate

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Doors

The doors are adjustable and are attached to the body with two hinges. 

The liftgate assembly is adjustable and pivots on two removable hinges 
assisted by two gas-filled support cylinders.

The sliding door is adjustable and is attached to the body by three 
hinges.

At regular service intervals, the doors should be checked for proper 
operation. If the hinges, lock mechanisms, lock cylinders or door lock 
strikers are worn, replace them. Lubrication of the door locks and hinges is 
necessary to ensure trouble-free service.

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Weatherstrips, Aerostar 

 Removal 

Cut or separatefront door opening weatherstrip (20709) andrear door 
body weatherstrip (253A10) around opening at seam. 

Loosen and pry away from body flange with a flat tool such as a putty 
knife or equivalent.

Pull front door opening weatherstrip and rear door body weatherstrip 
outward and away from flange working upward, along the top, and around the 
opening. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Do not stretch weatherstrip during installation. 

Clean any residual adhesive or material from flange or body surface by 
scraping carefully with a flat tool such as a putty knife or wipe with a cloth 
using Extra Strength Tar and Road Oil Remover B7A-19520-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M5B106-A. 

Start installation at the proper area indicated in the illustration. 
Compress the front door opening weatherstrip and rear door body weatherstrip 
onto the flange and continue working across or around the opening. 

Insert sponge plug into loose end of front door opening weatherstrip and
rear door body weatherstrip. 

Cut front door opening weatherstrip andrear door body weatherstrip, if 
necessary, 6-12mm longer than required and butt ends together. Avoid 
overlapping. 

To install roof side rail weatherstrip (51222), apply Weatherstrip 
Adhesive E8AZ-19552-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G14-A to 
forward pushpin only if required.

Insert pushpin near front at paint mark, then work outward and rearward 
installing weatherstrip carrier onto flange.

Peel protective backing off adhesive tape at rear molded seal or where 
required. 

Aerostar body lock pillar cover installation should be started at top, 
then down lock pillar with adhesive tape protective backing removed, ending 
above the rocker panel. 

Installation of back door opening weatherstrip assembly is same as body 
door openings. Clean surfaces with alcohol before applying adhesives. Remove 
protective backing from adhesive tape where required and apply pressure to 
installed assembly at these areas.

 Removal and Installation

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Tailgate, Ranger 

 Removal and Installation 

Open tailgate. 

Partially close tailgate to relieve tension on the tailgate check cables 
(43052). Pull up on cable retainer spring and slidetailgate check cable 
retainer to large opening in the hook and lift off. Repeat for other tailgate 
check cable. 

Hold tailgate approximately half open position (45 degrees) and lift 
off the right hinge. Pull tailgate along its axis. 

Move tailgate to the right to remove from left hinge. 

For installation, follow removal procedures in reverse order. If a new 
tailgate is being installed, transfer all moulding, latches, hinges, brackets, 
cables, links, clips, washers, and any other hardware to new tailgate. 
Lubricate hinge cups, each side, with Multi-Purpose Grease D0AZ-19584-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C93-A.

ADJUSTMENTS

Front Door Alignment

 CAUTION: Do not cover up a poor door alignment with a latch striker adjustment.

desired direction. Mark hinge with pen or pencil for reference point.

a padded pry bar.

desired fit.

Tighten bolts to specifications.

the adjacent panel. 

Repeat the operation until the desired fit is obtained.

Check the striker plate alignment for proper door closing. Refer to 
 Section 01-14A for striker adjustment.

ADJUSTMENTS

Sliding Door Alignment, Aerostar

 CAUTION: For proper sliding door operation it is critical that the door adjuster 
wedge and striker on the front face of the sliding door fit smoothly into the 
wedge pocket and plate located in the B-pillar. If any of the following 
adjustments are made, re-alignment of the wedge and striker may be necessary. 

 In or Out Adjustment 

 NOTE: Support the sliding door to prevent up or down movement during 
adjustment.

 Front Upper 

To adjust the front of the sliding door, loosen two nuts retaining the 
body side door bracket assembly to the upper guide roller assembly.

Move the roller assembly in or out as required to obtain a flush fit of 
the door to body.

[FIGURE: N5980C.gif]

 Front Lower 

Mark surface before loosening adjusting nut. Adjust lower front edge of 
the sliding door by loosening the adjusting nut on the lower guide assembly 
and move the door in or out as required to obtain a flush fit. The lower guide 
vertical roller is a load bearing roller and should roll easily within the 
lower track as the sliding door is opened or closed.

Vertical adjustment of lower guide is accomplished by loosening three 
bolts and moving base of guide.

If vertical adjustment is made to lower guide, inspect the upper guide 
to make sure the upper guide does not contact the bottom of the track housing 
or the upper guide roller contacts the top of the upper track.

[FIGURE: N59811A.gif]

 Striker Rear Latch 

 CAUTION: Striker adjusts in or out only. Up and down adjustment is obtained with 
rear hinge and lower front guide. 

The sliding door latch is located at the rear of the door. When the 
door is closed the latch engages the striker which positions the rear of the 
door to the body. Adjusting the striker in or out will position the rear edge 
of the sliding door as required to obtain the proper fit to the body.

 Striker Rear Latch, Aerostar 

[FIGURE: N5991B.gif]

 Hinge Assembly 

To adjust the sliding door fore or aft, loosen three bolts retaining 
the center door hinge to the door and adjust hinge fore or aft as required to 
secure a proper door fit.

Some up/down adjustment may be obtained from the center hinge by moving 
the center hinge strap up or down as desired prior to securing the retainer 
bolts.

The vertical hinge rollers within the body center track assembly must 
be parallel to the top of the track and maintain a minimum clearance of 1mm 
(0.040 inch) from the top of the track from smooth operation. If hinge is 
adjusted vertically, evaluate striker setting for fit and centering.

ADJUSTMENTS

Dual Rear Door Alignment, Aerostar

 CAUTION: Do not cover up poor rear door (24630) alignment with a latch striker 
adjustment. 

From inside of vehicle, remove plug button for hinge mounting driver 
access holes in pillar rear cover.

[FIGURE: R53091A.gif]

From inside the vehicle, loosen hinge screw and washer assembly just 
enough to permit movement of the door with a padded pry bar. Retain sliding 
door hinge and roller (26800) to body for side-to-side or up-and-down 
adjustments. 

Remove two screw and washer assemblies and loosen screw and washer 
assembly at the spacer slot location, retaining sliding door hinge and roller to
rear door, to remove or insert backdoor hinge spacer(s) for fore and aft 
adjustments.

for up and down or fore and aft adjustment. 

Loosen two screw and washer assemblies retaining lower hinge torear 
door for side to side adjustments. 

Adjust rear door, as necessary. Tighten screw and washer assemblies, 
and nut and washer assembly. 

Check the rear door fit to make sure there is no bind or interference 
with the adjacent panel. 

Repeat operation until desired fit is obtained in terms of flushness 
and gap. 

Check door latch striker plate (22008) alignment for proper rear door 
closing.

 Door Striker, Upper 

 NOTE: Use an M-11 socket to loosen or tighten the nut and washer assemblies

latch striker should not be adjusted to correct door sag. The latch striker 
should be shimmed to achieve correct clearance between latch striker and 
latch. To check this clearance, close one door at a time and observe the 
alignment as the latch engages the striker. Move the striker assembly fore and 
aft to provide a flush fit at the door and the body.

ADJUSTMENTS

Tailgate Gap, Ranger

 Pickup Box Corner Pillar 

Lower the tailgate and clean the rear corner pillar with alcohol in the 
area in which the filler will be installed.

Peel the protective tape from the back side of filler F37B-9941050/1-AA 
to expose the sticky surface and attach filler to the rear corner pillar as 
shown in the illustration. Be sure to align the notches in the filler with the 
sheet metal embossments for proper fit.

Repeat Steps 1 and 2 for opposite side of vehicle.

[FIGURE: N10742A.gif]

 Tailgate Inner Filler 

 CAUTION: Do not alter the size or shape of template. Changing template will 
impact its fit on tailgate. 

Trace and cut out template provided in this section.

Position template on upper side of tailgate in the area in which the 
tailgate filler will be installed.

Using template, center punch sheet metal in locations shown.

Remove template and drill two 1/4-inch holes at the center punch 
locations.

Apply a small amount of Superseal Anti-Corrosion Compound F3AZ-19515-SA 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M7C54-A to the sheet metal area 
that was drilled.

tailgate as shown.

Repeat the procedure for other side of vehicle.

LUBRICATION

Lubricant

 Weatherstrip, Door and Roof Side Rail 

Use Silicone Lubricant C0AZ-19553-AA (Jelly) or D7AZ-19553-AA (Spray) 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A on the door and window 
weatherstrips. It is recommended that silicone lubricant be applied to the 
weatherstrips whenever necessary. Silicone lubricant helps avoid weatherstrip 
squeaks, and retards excess weatherstrip wear caused by chafing between the 
door glass upper frame and the weatherstrip. It also helps to retain door 
window alignment by reducing friction between the glass frame and the rubber 
weatherstrip.

 Hinge, Door 

Use Multi-Purpose Grease Spray D7AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M1C93-A to lubricate door hinges.

[FIGURE: N6585B.gif]

 Hinge, Luggage Compartment Door 

Multi-Purpose Grease Spray D7AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESB-M1C93-A is used to lubricate luggage compartment door 
hinges. Apply an even coat to all movable hinge surfaces when a binding 
condition occurs.

LUBRICATION

Hinge, Tailgate

1997 Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Pickup Box Alignment

Loosen the six pickup box attaching bolts.

 NOTE: Make sure cab-to-box margin at outboard edge of box is no less than 
21.0mm (0.82 in.). Less than minimum clearance may result in cab-to-box 
contact during severe usage.

Move box so front of pickup box is centered on rear of cab.

If satisfactory alignment is achieved, tighten the six bolts to 53-72 Nm
 (40-53 lb-ft).

If satisfactory alignment cannot be achieved by following Steps 1-3, it 
may be necessary to adjust position of cab.

Loosen six cab mounting bolts.

 CAUTION: Make sure cab-to-box margin is no less than 21.0mm (0.82 in.). 

Move cab and pickup box to achieve proper alignment.

Tighten six pickup box bolts to 53-72 Nm (40-53 lb-ft).

Tighten four cab bolts to 68-92 Nm (50-68 lb-ft). 
Tighten front end sheet metal bolts to 68-92 Nm (50-68 
lb-ft). Tighten the nut on top of the front end sheet metal bolt to 46-64 Nm
 (34-47 lb-ft).

Adjust the transmission shift select cable. Refer to Transmission Shift 
Control Cable and Bracket under Adjustments in Section 07-05 .

[FIGURE: N11781B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3497
================================================================================
1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-04: Pickup Box

1997 Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Pickup Box Lean

The following procedure may be used to eliminate pickup box lean.

Place vehicle on a flat, smooth surface.

Inspect vehicle for any heavy add-ons that may cause excessive weight 
on any corner of vehicle.

Vehicle should be empty, fuel tanks should be full, no cargo in the 
pickup box (such as tools, equipment or debris).

Vehicle must be sitting on the wheels and tires and not on a hoist, 
jack, or jackstands.

Check all wheels and tires.

Wheels must be same size and design, right and left side on each axle.

Tires must be same brand, tire size, tread design, and equal tread wear 
side-to-side on each axle.

Wheel size and design, tire size, and tire design should be indicated 
on the Vehicle Certification Label. Use of larger size, off-road, wide tread 
wheels and/or tires are not approved.

Check tire pressures of all tires; inflate to specifications indicated 
on the Vehicle Certification Label.

Lay a straightedge at least 2 meters (6-1/2 feet) long across the rear 
edge of the pickup box and have an assistant hold the straightedge.

[FIGURE: N11782A.gif]

Standing 2.0-2.5 meters (6-8 feet) behind the truck, with your eye 
level at the top of the pickup box, have your assistant lift whichever side of 
the straightedge is necessary to make it parallel to the back window of the cab.

 Measuring for Lean 

[FIGURE: N11783A.gif]

Measure the distance between the bottom of the straightedge and the top 
of the pickup box outer panel and shim the low side of vehicle as follows:

If the distance is between 0 and 6.35mm (0 and .25 in.), do nothing.

If the distance is between 6.60 and 17.78mm (.26 in. and .70 in.), shim 
the axle.

If the distance is greater than 17.78mm (.70 in.) but less than 30-48mm 
(1.20 in.), shim the pickup box.

If the distance is greater than 30.48mm (1.20 in.), shim both the axle 
and pickup box.

If any of these conditions exist, refer to Shimming procedures in this 
section.

If, after shimming, the rear bumper is not aligned with the rear of 
pickup box, re-align the bumper as follows:

Remove the four bumper-to-chassis frame attaching bolts.

Ream the four holes to 17mm (0.66 in.) (two each side) on the bumper 
arms through which the chassis frame attaching bolts are installed.

Reinstall the bumper to chassis frame attaching bolts and align the 
bumper to the pickup box.

Torque the bumper attaching bolts to 95-140 Nm (70-103 
lb-ft).

================================================================================
PAGE 3498
================================================================================
1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-04: Pickup Box

1997 Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Shimming

 Axle 

Measure the rear ride height by measuring the height of the right and 
left rear fender lip openings.

Compute the difference.

A side-to-side lean at the rear of the vehicle can be adjusted 
approximately 6mm (1/4 inch) by installing a shim between the rear spring 
(5560) and axle on the low side of the vehicle. 

A "low at the rear" vehicle can be raised approximately 6mm (1/4 inch) 
by installation of one shim on each side. 

Use the following procedure to install the shim(s) (E37A-5742-AA). 

Raise the vehicle until the weight is off the rear springs but with the 
tires still touching the floor. 

Loosen the spring U-bolts to allow the axle to separate from the spring 
approximately 13mm (1/2 inch). 

Position the shim (E37A-5742-AA) between the spring and the spring seat 
with the tie bolt head through the hole in the shim.

On 4x4 vehicles, position the shim between the rear spring and axle 
spacer. Tape may be used to hold the shim in position. 

Make sure the spring leaves are properly aligned and the spring U-bolts 
contact the edges of the spring assembly or axle seat. 

Tighten the spring U-bolt sufficiently and make sure the spring bolt 
head extends through shim into axle seat hole. 

Tighten the U-bolt nuts to 88-102 Nm (65-75 lb-ft). 

 Pickup Box 

Loosen all box attaching bolts. Remove the three bolts on the low side 
of the box.

1997 Ranger Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fabric

 Spot Cleaning 

Refer to Stain Cleaning in this section.

 Stain Cleaning 

 NOTE: For water soluble stains, use a damp cloth first, followed by a soft 
cloth with a mild detergent and water.

 Grease, Oil, Tar, Adhesive, Crayon and Lipstick 

Apply Ford Soil and Spot Lifter E8AZ-19526-A or equivalent to the 
soiled area.

Brush powder into fabric using delicate strokes on delicate fabrics. 
Use dry terry cloth on very delicate fabrics.

Allow cleaner to work at least 20 minutes, then vacuum powder.

Repeat if necessary.

If stain is still visible, complete the following steps:

Blot the stain with a clean, white cotton cloth that is saturated with 
Ford Spot and Stain Remover F3AZ-19521-WA or equivalent.

Rub in a circular motion, keeping a clean portion of the cloth in 
contact with the fabric.

Gradually widen the area as you rub. If a stain requires that a large 
amount of cleaner be used, clean the entire seat so a ring does not appear 
where the stain was.

Repeat, if necessary.

Wipe clean with a damp cloth to remove any remaining cleaner.

Allow the material to dry completely.

 Dirt, Dry Soil, Food and Beverages 

Apply Ford Extra Strength Upholstery Cleaner E8AZ-19523-AA, or 
equivalent, to the soiled area.

Scrub area with a damp cloth or sponge.

Gradually widen the area as you rub. If the stain requires that a large 
amount of cleaner be used, clean the entire seat so a ring does not appear 
where the stain was.

Repeat, if necessary.

Wipe immediately with a dry cloth.

Allow upholstery to dry completely before using.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Safety Belt Webbing

Clean the safety belt webbing with any cleaner recommended for cleaning

1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-05A: Trim, Interior, Ranger

1997 Ranger Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Plastic, Vinyl, and Leather

 NOTE: For cleaning leather surfaces, follow the procedures for cleaning vinyl 
and plastic surfaces.

For vinyl and plastic surfaces, remove dust and dirt with a whisk broom 
or vacuum. Clean the vinyl surfaces with Ford Deluxe Leather and Vinyl Cleaner 
E0AZ-19521-AA or equivalent, meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P4-A. Be 
careful of some cleaners which will change the gloss or shine of the vinyl and 
plastic surfaces.

For routine cleaning, wipe the surface with a soft, damp cloth.

For more thorough cleaning, wipe the surface with a soft cloth and mild 
detergent, or a vinyl cleaner such as Ford Deluxe Leather and Vinyl Cleaner 
E0AZ-19521-AA, or equivalent, meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P4-A. Do not 
use solvent-type cleaners such as spot remover or powder-type spot lifter on 
these materials.

Wipe the surface clean with a damp, soft cloth.

Dry and buff surface with a dry, soft cloth.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fabric

 NOTE: Using other than recommended cleaners or procedures may affect 
flammability or fabric appearance.

The following procedure is recommended for the removal of spots and 
stains encountered in service. It is important that proper cleaning techniques 
and cleaning agents be used to prevent the stain from setting or affecting the 
color and/or flame resistant properties of the fabric.

Remove excess staining material from fabric by scraping or wiping with 
a clean cloth (blot if stain is wet).

Identify the staining material if possible.

Clean the fabric as described below.

 Spot Cleaning 

 Grease, Oil, Tar, Water Spots, Crayon and Lipstick 

 CAUTION: Care should be used in application of the spot lifter to prevent it 
from contacting vinyl trim. 

Spray stain with Extra Strength Upholstery Cleaner E8AZ-19523-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications from a distance of 203-254mm (8-10 
inches) as directed on the instructions furnished with the can.

Allow the spot lifter to dry completely, forming a white powder on the 
surface of the fabric.

Brush and vacuum the white powder from the surface of the fabric.

If the soiled spot is not removed from the fabric repeat Steps 1, 2 and 
3 as necessary.

 Stain Cleaning 

Spot cleaning as described above will be sufficient on fabrics which 
are not excessively soiled. However, to maintain a uniform appearance of the 
seat material in the event of severe soil and stain, the entire seat or insert 
will have to be cleaned to prevent a "ring" condition.

 Grease, Oil, Tar, Adhesive, Crayon and Lipstick 

If the stain is still visible after the spot cleaning procedure, blot 
the soiled area with a clean cotton cloth saturated with Extra-Strength Spot 
and Stain Remover F3AZ-19521-WA.

Rub in a circular motion while continuously exposing clean portion of 
cloth.

Gradually widen area of application onto edges of design, pleat, or 
biscuit.

Repeat Steps 1, 2 and 3 as necessary.

Wipe cleaned area with clean damp cloth to remove any residual cleaner.

 Dirt, Dry Soil, Food and Beverages 

Apply Rosenthal or Bissell or an equivalent upholstery cleaner with 
clean brush or sponge as directed on the instructions furnished with the 
container.

Rub in a circular motion until stain is removed.

Gradually widen area of application to edges of design, pleat, or 
biscuit.

Repeat Steps 1, 2 and 3 as necessary.

Rub cleaned area with a damp cloth to absorb residual cleaner.

Allow to dry at room temperature.

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Adhesive Removal/Repair Body Side Mouldings/Nameplates 

Completely clean sheet metal surface area around moulding using 
isopropyl alcohol and a clean soft cloth.

Before removing moulding, mark moulding location on top and each end of 
moulding with masking tape. Do not heat moulding or sheet metal surface; this 
only increases the adhesion. Temperatures of -18°C (0°
F) and below allow easier removal of moulding.

[FIGURE: N56861A.gif]

Using a nylon wedge tool, start at rear of door and wedge tool between 
moulding and door. At the same time, pull moulding away with steady tension. 
Remove and replace one moulding at a time. 

Once a few inches of moulding are free, grip moulding with both hands 
and pull the moulding slowly toward the front of vehicle, being careful not to 
damage paint or sheet metal surface. 

 NOTE: Not all of the tape will come off with moulding; white or gray acrylic 
tape is most easily removed by gently stretching.

Grip tape at one end, lifting and pulling away slowly about 12mm (0.5 
inch) at a time; then grip and pull again. Small pieces can be removed by 
rolling with thumb across sheet metal surface. 

When all tape is removed, wipe area with isopropyl alcohol and clean 
soft cloth, making sure all tape residue and road dirt is removed. A clean 
surface is required for application of new moulding. Should paint surface be 
damaged during moulding removal, surface should be repaired using paint repair 
procedure. 

 NOTE: Mouldings should not be installed on vehicle unless sheet metal surface 
temperature exceeds 27°C (80°F) and moulding 
is at 21°C (70°F) minimum. 

New moulding is now ready to be applied. Start at front of door 
moulding, pull back tape protective liner approximately 19mm (0.75 inch). Do 
not touch or contaminate tape surface. Line moulding up with marks on masking 
tape at rear of door and press gently forward on door, removing protective 
liner as you proceed forward. Be sure part is lined up correctly.

Remove masking tape and wipe area under masking tape with isopropyl 
alcohol to remove residue. 

Press moulding on with hand roller applying a minimum of 138 kPa (20 
psi) pressure to assure positive tape adhesion.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mirror, Outside Rearview, Power

The outside rear view mirror control (17B676) for the dual electric 
mirrors is located in the upper front area of the front door trim panel 
(23942). The same outside rear view mirror control controls both the left and 
right outside rear view mirrors (17682). 

Mirror position may be adjusted by first moving the selector switch to 
the L or R position. Then, adjust the outside rear view mirrors by pressing 
the appropriate arrow. 

When not adjusting, the outside selector switch should be kept in 
center OFF position to avoid inadvertent adjustment.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify the concern by operating the outside rear view mirrors.

Visually inspect for obvious signs of mechanical and electrical damage; 
refer to the following chart.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged mirrors.

Damaged remote control mirror switch.

Blown fuse:

No. 1 (7.5 Amp) (Ranger)

No. 8 (15A) (Aerostar)

Damage to wiring harness.

Loose or corroded connections.

If the visual inspection reveals no obvious concerns; refer to the 
following Symptom Chart.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mirror Mounting Bracket, Inside Rearview Mirror

Locate and mark the location ofinside rear view mirror bracket (17698) 
on the outside surface of the windshield glass (03100) with a wax pencil.

If the clear vinyl wafer remained on the windshield glass, apply low 
heat (heat gun) until the wafer softens. Peel the vinyl wafer from the 
windshield glass taking care not to scratch or mar the windshield glass 
surface. 

Thoroughly clean inside of the windshield glass with mild abrasive 
cleaning powder and clean cloth saturated in alcohol to remove old adhesive. 
Then, use a paper towel and remove all cleaner from the windshield glass. Do 
not contaminate clean area. Roughen the bonding surface of the inside rear 
view mirror bracket with fine grit sandpaper. Then, wipe the surface clean 
with a paper towel soaked in alcohol. Do not contaminate cleaned bracket. 

If vinyl wafer is still adhered to theinside rear view mirror bracket, 
use low heat (heat gun) until the wafer softens and peel it off. 

Use fine sandpaper on inside rear view mirror bracket to lightly scuff 
the surface. Wipe clean with alcohol-moistened cloth. 

 CAUTION: Do not touch the mounting surfaces. 

Using the applicator, apply a generous amount of Rearview Mirror 
Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G176-A 
to the bonding surface of the inside rear view mirror bracket and the 
windshield glass. Allow the adhesive material to dry for three minutes. 

Apply two drops of Rearview Mirror Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G176-A to the mounting surface of the inside 
rear view mirror bracket. Using a clean toothpick or wooden match, quickly 
spread the adhesive evenly over the mounting surface of the inside rear view 
mirror bracket. 

Quickly position the inside rear view mirror bracket on the windshield 
glass, using the locator marked on the outside of the windshield glass. The 
9.525mm (3/8-inch) circular depression in the inside rear view mirror bracket 
must be down and toward the inside of the passenger compartment. Press the 
inside rear view mirror bracket against the windshield glass for about one 
minute. 

Allow the adhesive to set for five minutes. Then remove any excess 
adhesive material from the windshield glass with an alcohol-dampened rag.

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seats, Front 

The front seats (60012) are mounted on two front seat tracks (61705), 
which allow fore and aft movement. The front seat tracks are mounted to a 
support assembly which is mounted to the floor of the vehicle. 

 Power, Six-Way, Ranger 

The optional six-way power seat system uses a screw-type drive for 
adjusting front seats.

The six-way power seat provides horizontal, vertical and tilt 
adjustments. It consists of a reversible armature motor, switch and housing 
assembly, vertical linkage, and horizontal screw drives. 

The mechanical portion of the front seat track in the horizontal drive 
consists of a transmission and lead screw on each track. The transmission, 
lead screw and motor are attached to the movable section of the track. 

When the seat regulator control switch (14A701) is actuated forward or 
rearward, the front armature is energized and the horizontal drive units are 
activated. The seat is then moved forward or rearward by the lead screw 
traveling in a plastic drive block attached to each lower front seat track 
section. 

In the vertical drive, a transmission and link drive are used. The 
drive units are located on the left side of the front seat track. 

When the seat regulator control switch is actuated up or down, the 
center and rear armatures are energized simultaneously and the vertical drive 
units are activated. The seat is then moved up or down by the lead linkage 
rotated by the torsion bar.

When the seat regulator control switch is actuated, the center armature 
drives the front vertical linkage and moves the seat to the desired position. 
When the seat regulator control switch is actuated, the rear armature drives 
the rear vertical torsion bar and moves the seat to the desired position. 

The power seat circuit is protected by a circuit breaker mounted in the 
fuse panel. 

The seat regulator motor (14547), which contains three armatures, the 
flexible shafts, the screw drive and gear mechanism are not serviced 
individually and can be serviced only by replacing the complete track 
assembly. 

 Circuit Protection 

The power seat circuit is protected by a 20-amp circuit breaker. The 
circuit breaker is mounted in the fuse panel.

================================================================================
PAGE 3576
================================================================================
1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seat Tracks

 Manual 

The seat release handle is located at the front of the seat. Pulling 
the seat release handle allows forward or rearward movement of the seat 
assembly.

Manual seat tracks are retained to the floorpan by bolt and washer 
assemblies at both rear positions and at the front outboard position. The 
bolts retaining the seat tracks are removed from inside the vehicle.

 Tilt Slide Seat 

The tilt slide seat can be moved forward and backward on a track. With 
the seat back tilted forward, the tilt slide seat can be moved forward to 
provide additional entry space to access the rear seat compartment of the 
vehicle.

A tilt slide allows the seat to be moved forward to provide additional 
entry space for access to the right rear compartment. To operate, activate the 
seat back handle, located on the outboard side of the seat. The seat will move 
forward. To return the seat rearward, keep seat back in forward position and 
push seat cushion assembly rearward to the desired position. Return the seat 
back to the upright position to lock the seat into place.

 NOTE: Any position on the track, in which the seat back is returned to the 
upright position will lock the seat location.

1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seat, Center

 Built-In Child Seat 

The rear seat of vehicle may be equipped with an optional built-in 
child seat. To utilize the child seat, pull the headrest release strap. Then 
release the strap and pull the headrest to the full up position, until the 
headrest latch clicks. Lower the child seat cushion. Make sure to read all 
safety and warning information provided on the child seat cushion protector 
flap. Adjust lap/shoulder belt and crotch belt buckle according to the child's 
size, comfort, and safety.

Children must be properly buckled before riding in the vehicle. It is 
the law in every state and province. This child seat conforms to all 
federal/Canadian motor vehicle safety standards.

Frequently check the child seat lap and shoulder harness belts for 
correct placement and tightness. Use only if the harness belts can be pulled 
snug and will stay snug. If not, take the child seat to the dealer for repair.

Prior to using the built-in child seat, refer to your owner guide for 
proper usage guidelines and safety requirements.

 WARNING: ALL BUILT-IN CHILD RESTRAINTS, INCLUDING SEATS, BUCKLES, RETRACTORS, 
SEAT LATCHES, INTERLOCKS, AND ATTACHING HARDWARE SHOULD BE INSPECTED BY A 
QUALIFIED DEALER TECHNICIAN AFTER ANY COLLISION. IF THE CHILD SEAT WAS IN USE 
DURING A COLLISION, FORD RECOMMENDS REPLACING IT. HOWEVER, IF THE COLLISION 
WAS MINOR AND A QUALIFIED TECHNICIAN FINDS THAT THE CHILD RESTRAINTS DO NOT 
SHOW DAMAGE AND CONTINUE TO OPERATE PROPERLY, THEY DO NOT NEED TO BE REPLACED. 
BUILT-IN CHILD SEATS NOT IN USE DURING A COLLISION SHOULD ALSO BE INSPECTED 
AND REPLACED IF EITHER DAMAGE OR IMPROPER OPERATION IS NOTED.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lumbar Support System, Ranger

The lumbar support system consists of the seat back control switch, 
front seat back pad adjuster (65500), a pump and motor assembly, related 
wiring harness and plastic tubing. 

During the inflate mode, the front seat back pad adjusting pump (65530) 
pumps air through a front seat back pad adjusting hose (65528) to the lumbar 
switch check valve. 

The air is then routed through a separate hose to the front seat back 
pad adjuster lumbar support located at the seat back. 

Except for the front seat back pad adjuster, all components are located 
at or under the front cushion pad.

The seat back control switch performs three functions. 

First, it turns the front seat back pad adjusting pump on. 

Second, it is a one-way check valve for air passage to the front seat 
back pad adjuster. Once the bag is inflated and the seat back control switch 
is left to its normal mode, the check valve closes and prevents air in the bag 
from leaking out. 

Third, in the deflate mode, it opens the check valve, releasing the air 
deflating the front seat back pad adjuster. In this mode thefront seat back 
pad adjusting pump does not operate.

The longer nipple on the seat back control switch (located at the 
center of the seat regulator control switch (14A701)) should always be 
connected to the front seat back pad adjusting hose leading to the front seat 
back pad adjuster. The shorter nipple on the seat back control switch connects 
to the air pump outlet. If this order is reversed, the front seat back pad 
adjuster will not hold air pressure.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Recliner, Manual

The reclining front seat back (64811) is adjusted by a adjuster handle 
on the side of the seat cushion. To recline the seat back, lift the adjuster 
handle upward, push the seat back to the desired position, and release the 
handle. Spring action will return the seat back to its full-up position when 
the handle is released and occupant back pressure is removed. 

An entirely modular recliner mechanism is located on the outboard rear 
corner of the front seat (60012) and also provides the seat back pivot. This 
type of front seat back latch (62648) is used on bucket seats (also 60/40 seat 
on Ranger SuperCab) and is released by an adjuster handle on the outboard side 
of the seat cushion frame.

Some rear seats have a seat back recliner assembly. To recline the rear 
seat back lift the rear seat back latch handle (62418) upward, push the seat 
back to the desired position, and release the handle. Spring action will 
return the seat back to its full-up position when the rear seat back latch 
handle is released and occupant back pressure is removed.

If a recliner assembly or component is nonfunctional or damaged, the 
entire recliner assembly must be replaced.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Test

 Folding Bench Seats with Inertia Latch Assemblies, Ranger 

In the event the front seat back latch (62648) does not pass the 
functional check, the entire front seat back latch must be replaced. Service 
of the components is not acceptable and should not be attempted. 

With the seat installed in the vehicle, push down and hold the adjuster 
handle. Tilt the front seat back latch forward until it is in a vertical 
position. 

Grasp the front seat back (64811) and bounce it against its rear stop 
while holding the adjuster handle (62622) down (the front seat back will 
bounce forward from the stop, momentarily engaging the front seat back latch, 
and then return to its normal rearward position). 

 NOTE: The following check verifies that the front seat back latch pawl 
(62606) is free to move and lock-up (for folding seat backs with inertia latch 
assemblies). 

Hold the front seat back and jerk it forward as soon as it contacts and 
bounces from the rear stop. The front seat back will now be restricted from 
tilting full forward.

With the front seat cushion and with the front seat back latch removed 
from the vehicle and supported in a horizontal position, the upper portion of 
the front seat back latch should be free to rotate and not be engaged by the 
lower portion. 

Rotate the front seat cushion with the front seat back latch forward 37 
degrees from the horizontal, and rotate the movable portion of the front seat 
back latch up into the latched position.

The movable portion must engage the lower fixed portion of the front 
seat back latch and remain engaged.

 Latch Sensitivity Test, Bench Seat with Inertia Latch 

In the event the above checks cannot be satisfactorily performed, the 
following sensitivity test must be made prior to replacing suspect latch 
assemblies. 

 NOTE: For bench seat applications, remove the inboard safety belt attachments. 

Remove the front seat (60012) and front seat track (61705) from the 
vehicle.

With the front seat and front seat track, positioned on a flat surface, 
slowly tilt the front seat forward enough to cause the front seat back to tilt 
forward (through gravity). 

The front seat back latch should engage at this point (11 degrees from 
original front seat back position), restricting the front seat back from 
tilting to its full forward position.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Seat, Driver, Front, Aerostar

 Removal and Installation 

Remove screw attaching front seat track (61705) to floor insulator.

Remove the three front seat-to-floor support attaching bolts and one 
seat belt bolt.

Remove the front seat (60012) from vehicle.

Position the front seat upside down on a clean bench.

Remove four nuts attaching seat support-to-front seat track. Remove 
seat support from front seat.

To remove the front seat track to floor insulator, disconnect the front 
set track latch tie rod from both front seat tracks.

Remove four attaching screws. Remove both front seat tracks from the 
front seat.

For installation, follow removal procedures in reverse order.

Tighten screws that hold front seat track to floor insulator to front 
seat cushion frame (60326) 15-20 Nm (11-15 lb-ft).

Tighten nuts attaching seat support to front seat track to 19-26 Nm
 (14-19 lb-ft).

Tighten bolts attaching front seat to floor support to 19-26 Nm
 (14-19 lb-ft).

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Seats, Rear Two- and Three-Passenger Bench and Bed, Aerostar 

 Removal 

Disengage the lap/shoulder seat belt from the seat by inserting a key 
or a small screwdriver into the slot in the detachable anchor and lifting 
upward. Stow the tongue end of the detachable anchor. 

On bench seat, fold seat back forward and latch it in the down position. 

Rotate the adjuster handles (located under seat near floor) upward 
simultaneously to disengage latch hooks from floor attachment. 

Lift seat at rear and rotate about the forward attachment. When 
adjuster handles are clear of floor attachments, release the adjuster handles.

Pull the seat rearward to disengage it from the front floor pins. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Care should be taken when storing seats out of the vehicle so the 
latches are not damaged. 

 WARNING: WHEN REINSTALLING A REAR SEAT IN YOUR VEHICLE IT MUST BE PLACED IN ITS 
ORIGINAL POSITION. IMPROPER INSTALLATION OF THE SEAT WILL PREVENT CORRECT USE 
OF THE SAFETY BELTS AND COULD INCREASE THE RISK AND/OR SEVERITY OF INJURY IN 
AN ACCIDENT. REFER TO THE WARNING LABEL ON THE SAFETY BELT. 

With the seat back in a folded and latched position (bench seat only), 
place the seat assembly in your vehicle and engage the front seat hooks onto 
the forward attachment pin in the floor wells. 

Rotate the seat downward and engage the rear seat back latch handle 
(62418) into the rear floor attachment. Lifting of the adjuster handles is not 
required for installation. 

Make sure that the adjuster handles are fully seated in the down 
position. 

Before you engage the safety belt, be sure it is not twisted. Remove 
any twist, then insert the tongue end of the detachable anchor into the 
detachable anchor until you hear a "snap" and feel the latch engage.

Latch, Bench, Front, Ranger

If the front seat back latch (62648) does not pass the sensitivity test, the entire front seat back latch must be replaced. Servicing components 
is not acceptable and should not be attempted. 

 Removal 

Remove front seat (60012) and front seat track (61705) as described in 
Removal and Installation, Seats, Front, Bench, Ranger in this section. 

Disengage front seat cushion and cover (60052) as required to gain 
access to screws retaining front seat back frame to front seat cushion and 
cover. Remove screws.

Disengage front seat back frame as required to gain access to nuts 
securing front seat back latch to seat back. Remove front seat back latch.

 Installation

retaining nuts and tighten to 18-27 Nm (13-20 lb-ft).

Install seat back trim cover.

cover. Tighten screws to 47-63 Nm (35-46 lb-ft).

Install seat cushion trim cover.

 NOTE: After front seat back latch replacement, the front seat must be tested 
in accordance with the latch sensitivity test procedure prior to installing 
the front seat in the vehicle.

Check front seat back latch for proper operation. Refer to front seat 
back latch sensitivity test.

Install seat and track assembly in vehicle as described in Removal and 
Installation, Seats, Front, Bench, Ranger in this section.

Check front seat tracks, front seat back latch and safety belts for 
proper operation. Upon replacement be sure to tighten the retaining

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Head Restraints, Front Seat Back, Ranger

 Removal and Installation 

Raise front seat back head restraint to maximum height stop.

With finger, depress the seat upholstery fabric around the sleeve to 
locate the hairclip under guide sleeve flange.

 NOTE: Guide sleeve may be oriented 180° from illustrated 
guide sleeve. Pull only on the rearmost leg of hairclip, which is the one 
engaging the height adjustment notches.

With finger or suitable tool, pull rearmost leg of hairclip rearward 
while lifting straight up on front seat back head restraint. This will 
disengage the last notch on the front seat head restraint guide rod sleeve.

Repeat for other front seat head restraint guide rod sleeve.

Lift front seat back head restraint to remove.

For installation, follow removal procedures in reverse order.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Seats and Tracks

 Unless otherwise noted, the disassembly and assembly 
illustrations shown in this section are typical of all seats. If some 
of the steps do not apply to the particular vehicle being serviced, proceed to 
the next step and review the appropriate illustration shown. 

Seat trim replacement requires removal and installation of seat 
components such as seat support bolt insulators, tracks and floor supports, 
and seat belts. 

For safety belt removal and installation procedures, refer to Section 01-20A .

 NOTE: Repairs to seat cushions or seat backs are performed out of the vehicle 
and are usually limited to replacement of torn or burned seat covers. In a few 
instances, the pads may be damaged and require replacement. 

When installing new seats or cushions and covers, refer to the 
applicable illustration for the location of listing wires, hog rings, 
anti-squeak pads, and seat pad stack-up.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Seat, Bench, Cushion Cover, Front

 Disassembly and Assembly 

Remove the front seat track (61705) from the vehicle. 

Remove front seat back head restraint. Refer to Removal and 
Installation, Head Restraints, Front Seat Back in this section.

Remove the front seat back (64811) from the front seat cushion frame 
and spring (63101). 

Cut the hog rings and/or disengage plastic retainers, and/or disengage 
hook-loop retaining the front seat cushion and cover to the front seat cushion 
frame and spring and remove the cover. 

If the front seat cushion pad is being replaced, cut the hog rings that 
attach the front seat cushion pad to the front seat cushion frame and spring 
(63100). Remove the padding. 

Position the new front seat cushion pad to the front seat cushion frame 
and spring and fasten it in place with hog rings. 

Transfer the listing wires to the new front seat cushion frame and 
spring. 

Position the front seat cushion frame and spring over the front seat 
cushion frame and spring. Fasten the front seat cushion frame and spring with 
hog rings and/or plastic retainers, and/or hook and loop. 

Install the front seat back to the front seat cushion frame and spring. 

Install the front seat (60012) and front seat track into the vehicle. 
Tighten the attaching screws and washers to specifications.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Seat, Back Cover and/or Pad, Bucket Seat, Rear, Aerostar

 Disassembly

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Latch, Inertia

The inertia latch assembly is factory-installed in its proper location. 
Customer or dealer maintenance is not required. Proper latch function in 
emergency situations requires that the seat back be in its full rearward 
normal position and against the rearward stops in the latch assembly. 
Therefore, the area behind the seat must be kept clear at all times to allow 
full rearward travel of the seat back. In addition, rear seat passengers 
should not lean on the front seat backs while the vehicle is in motion. The 
forward force on the seat back from the rear passenger in an emergency 
situation may prevent proper operation of the inertia latch mechanism.

 NOTE: The front seat back latch assembly release knob is not reusable. If it 
is removed, it must be replaced with a new knob.

================================================================================
PAGE 3628
================================================================================
1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Seats

The seat adjustment lever is located at the left front of the seat 
cushion. Pulling the lever to the left releases the lock mechanism, and the 
front seat (60012) can be adjusted fore and aft as required.

On Aerostar vehicles, the passenger seat mounts directly to the support 
assembly and is not adjustable.

On Ranger vehicles, release tension of the bench seat track latch can 
be adjusted by turning the turnbuckle located on the tie wire under the seat.

ADJUSTMENTS

Latch, Seat Back 

Front seat back latches are modular and do not require adjustments or 
maintenance.

================================================================================
PAGE 3630
================================================================================
1997 Aerostar/Ranger

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Aerostar, Ranger Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Seat Back, Reclining 

Recliner systems are modular and do not require customer or dealer 
adjustment or maintenance. In the event of hesitant or slow return of the seat 
back, lubrication of the recliner mechanism and the power spring of the 
assembly only is suggested with Ford Multi-Purpose Grease D7AZ-19584-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-A or ESB-M1C93-A. 

 NOTE: On Ranger Regular Cab, adding lubrication to the bench seat inertia 
latch mechanism will adversely affect the normal inertia function by impeding 
the free rotation of the locking cams. DO NOT lubricate the inertia latch. 

The only authorized service actions permitted on the recliner 
mechanisms are the tightening of all attaching screws to specification, the 
total replacement of a damaged or non-functional recliner, removal of any 
foreign material from the recliner (i.e., the strap, pieces of foam and trim, 
etc.), and proper lubrication of a hesitant seat back return recliner 
assembly.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Windshield Glass

The windshield glass (03100) is a standard plastic and glass laminate 
safety glass. Urethane sealant bonds the windshield glass to the window 
opening flange. The windshield glass also serves as a mount for the inside 
rear view mirror (17700).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Windows, Manual

The manually operated door windows are held in molded weather seals set 
into the door window opening channel. The door windows are raised and lowered 
by the door window regulators. The door window regulators are a cable and drum 
or geared mechanism operated by the window regulator handle.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window Regulator Control Switch

The power windows only operate with the ignition switch in the RUN or 
ACCY position.

The window regulator control switches control the actuation of the 
window regulator electric drives. Pressing on the raised portion of the window 
regulator control switch causes the window to move upward. Pressing on the 
depressed area of the window regulator control switch causes the window to 
move downward.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window, One-Touch Driver's Side, Ranger

 NOTE: The one-touch window feature can also be toggled on or off during the 
active test mode. Refer to Active Test Modes in Section 18-04A .

When the power switch for driver window control is held down (between 
0.04 and 0.4 seconds) and then released with the ignition switch (11572) in 
RUN or ACCY, the driver window will automatically move to its full down 
position.

Only the driver window has this feature. Holding the driver switch down 
longer allows the operator to stop the window as soon as the switch is released.

door window glass may be raised and lowered either manually or electrically 
(if equipped).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window, Heated Backlite and Mirror Timer 

The heated rear window defroster system consists of a heated back 
window switch assembly mounted on the instrument panel, a series of grid lines
